summary.one_liner: An awesome-style curated list of open source SQLite tools, language bindings, admin GUIs, schemas, books and related projects, maintained by Planet Open Data.
summary.what_it_does: This is a link list rather than software. It is organized by section: SQLite HQ and history, books, extensions (sqlean, TFR4SQLite), derivatives (sql.js), distributed variants (rqlite), middleware (ODBC and JDBC drivers), language bindings (R, Ruby, .NET, VBA, Swift), and admin tools split into web and desktop. Further sections cover SpatiaLite, text-to-SQLite converters (q, csvs-to-sqlite, datapak), PostgreSQL-to-SQLite migration, applications, misc utilities (litestream, cr-sqlite, sqliteproof, silentdrop), schema documentation generators, ready-made sample schemas (football.db, beer.db, Chinook, Northwind), and JSON API publishers (Datasette, SQLPage). Entries give a short description and sometimes a GitHub, web, or package link. The README says the commercial/proprietary tools are on a separate page.
use_cases: find a SQLite browser or admin GUI
find language bindings or drivers for SQLite
expose a SQLite database as a JSON API
find sample SQLite databases for practice
find SQLite extensions for replication or spatial data
notable: Categorized directory of SQLite tools across many languages (Python, Ruby, R, .NET, Swift, Go, PHP, JavaScript)
Lists web-based and desktop SQLite admin tools with platform notes
Includes ready-to-use sample schemas such as Chinook and Northwind
Links to a separate commercial/proprietary tools page, so this list covers open source only
caveats: Curated link list only; it does not provide any software itself
Some linked entries are old or point to retired hosts such as codeplex and the 2013 release history is outdated
The README does not say how often the list is maintained
summary.license: The awesome list is dedicated to the public domain.
